brief: Create one clear single-page critical-thinking post explaining why correlation does not establish causation. Use a familiar example that shows a third factor can explain two things that happen together. Keep the claim accurate, concise, and useful; include a practical question readers can ask.
title: The Correlation Fallacy
supporting_copy: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents both rise in July. Ice cream doesn't cause drowning; the heat does. When two trends move together, ask: Is there a hidden third factor driving both?

Top section: The title in a bold, oversized serif typeface. Middle section: The main point centered in a clean, heavy sans-serif. Bottom section: The supporting copy in a lighter weight, justified text. Visual metaphor: Two separate, parallel rising lines (representing the trends) that both originate from a single, glowing orange circle (the third factor) placed at the bottom center. The lines should be thin and precise. No labels or extra text on the graphic; only the supplied Title, Main_point, and Supporting_copy.
caption: Stop assuming A caused B just because they happened at the same time. The most dangerous errors in decision-making happen when we ignore the hidden variable.
